_comment: PROVENANCE PIN for the vendored copy of sysw_vectors.json (C-4).
The vectors are GENERATED in the Rust primary and are the contract this Go
port is measured against. Until 2026-08-15 sysw/conformance_test.go and
gui/sysw_load_test.go read them straight out of a SIBLING CHECKOUT at
../../mnemonic-engrave/..., which the fork's CI never checks out -- so the
whole cross-implementation conformance suite skipped on the one machine
whose verdict gates a merge, on every push, and the suite still printed ok.
The escalation that would have turned that skip into a failure
(SYSW_REQUIRE_VECTORS=1) appeared nowhere under .github/. An escalation
nobody sets is a skip with paperwork.
So the file is vendored, the skip is gone, and this pin is what keeps the
copy honest -- the same standing convention every ported Go package here
already carries: a provenance pin naming the primary it tracks, updated on
every sync, so drift is auditable.
TO RE-SYNC: copy the file, then update `commit`, `file_commit` and `sha256`
from the primary checkout:
cp ../mnemonic-engrave/crates/me-cli/testdata/sysw_vectors.json sysw/testdata/
git -C ../mnemonic-engrave rev-parse HEAD
git -C ../mnemonic-engrave log -1 --format=%H -- crates/me-cli/testdata/sysw_vectors.json
sha256sum sysw/testdata/sysw_vectors.json
TestVendoredVectorsMatchTheirProvenancePin fails if sha256 and the file
disagree; TestVendoredVectorsAreInSyncWithThePrimary audits the copy against
the sibling checkout when one is present.
